source: NY State Regents/EI archive — Grade 4 Elementary-Level Science Test, Written Test, June 4, 2018
license: NY State Education Department released test — same license basis as prior NY G4 Science batches (2019/2021/2022) already merged into this pipeline; publicly posted past exam with official scoring key, no paywall or login.
why_this_admin: NY Grade 4 Science June 2018 was checked against the elementary archive index (nysedregents.org/grade4/science/home.html) and confirmed as an administration not already mined (2019, 2021, 2022 are already in research/pipeline/ny-g4-science-2019 / -2021 / -2022). No administration newer than 2022 exists in the archive for this test (archive runs 2004-2022, most recent is 2022, already mined) — 2018 is the next-nearest unmined year with full released item text and an official answer key, matching the round's priority-1 instruction to find any NOT-already-mined NY G4 Science administration.
structure: Part I: 30 multiple-choice questions (labeled A-D, one question #11 has only 3 choices A-C). Part II: 15 open-ended constructed-response questions (#31-45), no fixed single answer, requires written student response, no answer key value beyond a rubric — excluded per standing no-fixed-answer rule used in every prior round.

part_1_multiple_choice.notes: All 30 items have their full text captured directly (see 01-extracted-classified.json). Several items reference a diagram/photo (Q3 polar bear body structures, Q5 oak tree life cycle, Q9 eagle/rabbit, Q10 arctic bird summer/winter, Q16 moon phases over September, Q17 US weather map, Q23 waterfall photo, Q28 pulley diagram, Q29 spring scale diagram) — in every case the diagram's content was fully legible and restatable in text (e.g. 'a bird looks larger/fluffier in winter than summer', 'city X: snow, city Y: rain' for the weather map) without needing image interpretation beyond what a sighted human transcriber already did here. None required guessing unseen visual data (no topographic maps, no precise graph-reading, no scale/ratio measurement from an image) — the STAAR/MCAS precedent for deferring image-dependent items does not apply to any of these 30.

part_2_open_ended.deferred_reason: Constructed-response, no fixed single correct answer suitable for this pipeline's multiple-choice format — same exclusion rule applied to every prior NY G4 Science batch's Part II.
